answer: The falcon test I would run is Guaranteed national park guide licence with parks authority attestation: a licence the authority renews after guiding audits, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since a licence the authority renews after guiding audits takes calendar time as well as money — and the juniper is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The copper grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
